tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$STARK_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.doc: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$STARK_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

tools.name: job
tools.description: Manage background jobs started by bash. action=list lists your background jobs; action=output reads new output since the previous read (optionally wait); action=kill requests cancellation.

job_id.description: Job id returned by bash with run_in_background. Required for output/kill.

wait.description: With action=output: block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

reason.description: With action=kill: optional short reason, recorded in the log.

tools.doc: job(action, job_id?, wait?, timeout_ms?, reason?) — Manage bash background jobs: list | output | kill.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content. PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF files return inline image parts instead of text; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect images. Read-only agents may pass workspace=<id|name> to inspect a registered workspace.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

workspace.description: Read-only target: workspace id or exact name. Omit to use the current workspace. Writable agents cannot use this to escape their workspace.

tools.doc: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content. PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF files return inline image parts instead of text; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect images.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Apply a unified patch to one or more files atomically. Prefer it over multiple edit calls when a change spans several files or separated regions. Add File, Update File, Delete File, and Move to are supported. Every hunk is validated before writing. Paths must be relative.

input.description: Patch text. Start with *** Begin Patch and end with *** End Patch.

tools.doc: codex apply_patch semantics: all-or-nothing, exact context, no silent overwrite.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result is sampled across top-level entries and reports where the complete list was saved. Read-only agents may pass workspace=<id|name> to inspect a registered workspace.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

workspace.description: Read-only target: workspace id or exact name. Omit to use the current workspace. Writable agents cannot use this to escape their workspace.

tools.doc: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result is sampled across top-level entries and reports where the complete list was saved.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved. Read-only agents may pass workspace=<id|name> to inspect a registered workspace.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

workspace.description: Read-only target: workspace id or exact name. Omit to use the current workspace. Writable agents cannot use this to escape their workspace.

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

agent_type.description: Agent type override for the new agent. Omit unless explicitly asked. The selected role applies regardless of how much parent history is inherited.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

tools.doc: Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

tools.name: message_agent
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. By default the message is queued without starting a new turn; set wake=true to trigger a turn if the target is idle (delivered promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes).

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

wake.description: Trigger a turn if the target is idle. Defaults to false (queue only).

tools.doc: message_agent(target, message, wake?) — Queue a message; wake=true triggers an idle agent turn.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000. Prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

tools.doc: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.doc: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

tools.description: Close an agent and any open descendants when they are no longer needed, and return the target agent's previous status before shutdown was requested. tools.name: workspace
tools.description: Manage project workspaces (the folder registry in .deep_agents/workspaces.json). action=create makes a new folder under root, or registers an existing path, or clones a git repo with repo=; action=clone re-clones a registered workspace that is missing on this machine; action=list shows registered folders plus the virtual General/House/Personal/DFD workspaces; action=info looks one up by id, name, or path; action=remove unregisters it (files are never deleted, virtual workspaces cannot be removed). Results report the folder relative to the projects root, never an absolute path. Starting work stays in delegate / agent spawn / create_group — this tool never starts an agent or creates a chat.

action.description: create: new folder/repo or register path. clone: re-clone a missing registered workspace (needs its stored repo). list/info/remove as named.

name.description: Folder name for action=create. 1-64 chars; filesystem-safe — avoid '/', '\', '..', control characters, and leading dots. Use kebab-case or snake_case. Ignored unless creating by name.

root.description: Parent folder for action=create with name. Defaults to the projects root (STARK_PROJECTS_ROOT); must stay inside it. DFD agents must use a folder under the DFD clients root.

path.description: Existing folder to register (action=create), or a lookup for action=info. Must exist and be a directory when creating.

repo.description: Git repository to clone for action=create. Accepts owner/repo, github.com/owner/repo, HTTPS, SSH (git@...) or file:// URLs. The folder is cloned into root/name and the URL is stored so another machine can action=clone it later. Private repos need a deploy key on the server.

branch.description: Optional branch for repo clone (default: repository default branch).

workspace_id.description: Workspace id for action=remove (and preferred lookup for action=info).

query.description: Name, id, or path to look up for action=info. Falls back to workspace_id when omitted.

tools.doc: workspace(action, name?, root?, path?, repo?, branch?, workspace_id?, query?) — Registry primitive: create (mkdir, register path, or git clone via repo), clone (re-clone a missing registered workspace from its stored repo), list, info, remove (unregister only, never deletes files). Dispatch stays in delegate / agent spawn / create_group.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Maintain the plan dock. Call when jobs change (spawn, progress, abort). FULL REPLACEMENT each call: send every step with its current status; at most one in_progress. Settled jobs use status=completed — put the reason in the step text when not successful. For small tweaks use ops instead of resending everything (mutually exclusive with plan): [{op, match?, step?, status?}] with op=add (needs step) | set_status (needs match+status) | rename (needs match+step) | remove (needs match); match is a case-insensitive substring of the step text.

explanation.description: Short note shown above the plan (e.g. 'Spawned 3 jobs, waiting for results'). Keep to one line.

match.description: Case-insensitive substring of the step text (set_status/rename/remove).

step.description: Step text (add, or rename's new text).
Short, human-readable job description. For settled jobs, prefix the reason when not successful (e.g. 'Build snake game — failed: tests did not pass').

tools.doc: update_plan(explanation?, plan?, ops?) — Maintain the task plan. FULL replacement: always send every step (at most one in_progress), or patch small tweaks via ops=[{op: add|set_status|rename|remove, match?, step?, status?}] (mutually exclusive with plan).

tools.name: delegate
tools.description:
Spawn one or more workspace agents (Developer / General / House) IN PARALLEL. Every item gets its own visible chat; final replies arrive as [DELEGATION RESULT] events while you keep coordinating.

BRIEF — you define WHAT, never HOW. Each item carries outcome (what the user gets when it is done, in the user's terms) and acceptance (how success will be judged — observable evidence). Never prescribe libraries, frameworks, architecture, step lists, file-by-file plans, or design direction; the specialist is the pro and owns the method (it may deviate and must report deviations). Name a command in acceptance only if the user named it or it is the project's standard entry point; otherwise describe the behavior and let the specialist choose the proof. One or two lines each — if they get long, you are doing the specialist's job. Method reminders are added to the task automatically; do not write them yourself.

BATCHING — per user turn: put EVERY independent job from the current request into a SINGLE delegate(items=[...]) call. Any agent mix is allowed and runs in parallel — solo scope (just Developer, just General, or just House) or mixed (Developer + General, Developer + House, all three). The sole batching criterion is independence. If job B needs job A's output, do NOT bundle B with A: delegate A first, wait for its [DELEGATION RESULT], then delegate B with A's result in the task. Never split a single request across multiple delegate calls for tidiness or sequencing — one call, all independent items.

EFFORT — match effort to the request: one job for a simple ask, 2-4 for comparisons, more ONLY when directions are truly independent. Jobs beyond the parallel cap wait as 'queued' and start automatically — never flood the system.

RESULTS — each job's final reply arrives as a [DELEGATION RESULT] summary (plus its artifact path and, when set, acceptance). Drill into the full report with delegation_status(id=...) when needed; never paste reports into your reply.

CHAT CONTINUATION — chat_id is optional. Omit it for a new job (default). Set it ONLY when this item is a follow-up, correction, or bug on a chat you can identify from a prior [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session. If the chat_id you pass does not exist, the runtime silently starts a new chat — so never guess an id.

RESUME — project continues a REGISTERED project's durable Dev session instead of starting a new chat. When the request is a follow-up, bug fix, or new work on an EXISTING project and you have no chat_id from a prior [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session, pass project=<name> (agent must be Dev or omitted) instead of workspace/chat_id. The message goes to the project's durable Dev in its own project chat — nothing new is created — and the completion arrives as a [DELEGATION RESULT] like any other job. Unknown names return [NOT FOUND] with the available names — never guess. Omit project for genuinely new work.

agent.description: Target workspace agent. Developer builds/fixes software; General handles research, docs, images, personal notes/admin; House controls smart-home devices. Case-insensitive.

task.description: Complete, self-contained instruction: goal, relevant paths/targets, constraints. The agent sees only this text. Context, not method — do not prescribe step-by-step process (use outcome/acceptance for the WHAT).

outcome.description: What the user gets when this job is done — the visible result, in the user's terms, 1-2 sentences. WHAT, never HOW: no libraries, frameworks, architecture, step lists, or design direction. Real paths the user named are fine as targets; invented ones are not.

acceptance.description: How success will be judged — observable evidence (a behavior, a result, something that must exist or respond). Not internals. Name a command only if the user named it or it is the project's standard entry point. The specialist chooses how to meet and prove it.

timeout.description: Wall-clock seconds before the job is aborted and marked FAILED (default 3600; 0 = no limit). Fresh jobs only.

title.description: Short label for the delegation chat (e.g. 'Space game · Dev').

chat_id.description: Omit for a new chat. Set ONLY with a chat_id surfaced by an earlier [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session — never guess. Unknown ids silently start a new chat.

project.description: Registered project id or exact name (no fuzzy matching). Set this INSTEAD of workspace/chat_id to continue the project's durable Dev session in its own project chat — no new tab is created. Only with agent Dev (or omitted).

workspace.description: Workspace id or exact name. An ambiguous name returns the candidate ids instead of guessing. Omit to use the default: current project for Dev, General workspace for General, House workspace for House.

images.description: Absolute file paths of image attachments relevant to THIS item. Missing files are silently dropped, so only attach paths you have verified exist.

isolate.description: Force git worktree isolation for this delegation.

items.task: Build a snake game in Python with tests
items.title: Snake game · Dev
items.outcome: A playable snake game that starts with one command and keeps a high score.
items.acceptance: The game starts and is playable; the project's test command passes.

items.acceptance: Searching the journal for 'shipped v0.1' finds the note.

items.title: Login crash fix

tools.doc: delegate(items=[{agent, task, outcome?, acceptance?, timeout?, title?, chat_id?, project?, workspace?, images?}]) — Spawn Developer/General/House agents; each gets its own chat (project=<name> continues a registered project's durable Dev in its own chat instead). outcome/acceptance define WHAT success is — never method. Results arrive as [DELEGATION RESULT] summaries + artifact paths; drill in with delegation_status(id).

tools.name: delegation_status
tools.description: Snapshot only — not a polling tool. Delegation results arrive automatically as [DELEGATION RESULT] events. Call once only when the user asks for status or after a wait/timeout, then stop. Pass id for one job's evidence; wait_seconds should stay 0 unless the user explicitly asks to wait.

id.description: Job id (del-xxxx) for the full evidence bundle of one job. Omit for the board.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this long for a job before answering (default 0 = answer now).

status.description: Board filter: only show jobs in this state.

tools.doc: delegation_status(id?, wait_seconds?, status?) — one snapshot of this session's delegations. Results are event-driven; never poll. wait_seconds is opt-in and defaults to 0.

tools.name: job_message
tools.description: Steer a RUNNING delegation mid-flight when the user adds scope or changes direction. Fresh jobs: mirrored into the job chat + queued on its steering channel. Resume jobs: queued on the durable Dev child (FIFO). Only works while the job is running — otherwise delegate a follow-up. Never blocks.

job_id.description: Job id (del-xxxx) from delegate or delegation_status.

message.description: Steering message: the added scope or direction change.

tools.doc: job_message(job_id, message) — Steer a RUNNING delegation mid-flight (fresh: steering channel; resume: durable Dev FIFO). Running jobs only; never blocks.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel ONE running delegation when the user says stop. Fresh jobs: cooperative abort of the job chat. Resume jobs: interrupt of the durable Dev child. Settles the entry as CANCELLED and reports back as a [DELEGATION RESULT]. Already-settled jobs are a no-op.

job_id.description: Job id (del-xxxx) from delegate or delegation_status.

reason.description: One-clause reason shown in the wrap-up (default: cancelled by the user).

tools.doc: job_cancel(job_id, reason?) — Cancel ONE running delegation (fresh: abort; resume: interrupt). Reports back as [DELEGATION RESULT] CANCELLED.

tools.name: files_changed
tools.description: Stage 5 (advisory): list the most recent external file changes in the active workspace. The agent can call this to notice when the user (or another tool outside this run) edits a file. Does NOT invalidate the read cache or interrupt a running tool. Requires the optional `watchfiles` package; if not installed, returns a friendly 'not available' string.

tools.name: house_get_state
tools.description: Read the full house state: rooms, every device with its current state, scenes, energy and security summary. Call this first whenever the user asks about the house.
tools.doc: house_get_state() — Read the full house state: rooms, devices, scenes, energy, security. Call first for any house question.

tools.name: house_get_device
tools.description: Read one house device: current state, writable capabilities, room and online status. Use to check a device before or after actuating it.
tools.doc: house_get_device(device_id) — One device's state, capabilities, room, online status.

tools.name: house_set_device
tools.description: Control a house device. state keys depend on type: light {power, brightness 0-100, colorTemp 2200-6500}; thermostat {targetTemp 10-35, mode off|heat|cool|auto}; lock {locked}; plug {power}; blinds {position 0-100}; camera {recording}. Sensors are read-only.
tools.doc: house_set_device(device_id, state) — Actuate a device: light {power,brightness,colorTemp}, thermostat {targetTemp,mode}, lock {locked}, plug {power}, blinds {position}, camera {recording}. Sensors read-only.

tools.name: house_run_scene
tools.description: Activate a house scene (applies all its device actions at once). Available scenes are listed in house_get_state, e.g. scene-morning, scene-night, scene-away, scene-movie, scene-focus.
tools.doc: house_run_scene(scene_id) — Activate a scene (applies all actions at once).

tools.name: house_get_history
tools.description: Mock energy-usage history for one house device (hourly kWh series, up to 168 hours).
tools.doc: house_get_history(device_id, hours?) — Mock hourly kWh usage series for a device (max 168h).

tools.name: dfd_bridge
tools.description: Call the DFD Agency API through the agent bridge (NON-MONEY operations only): leads, orders, milestones, order notes, activities, client requests, projects, articles, WhatsApp progress messages. Never use for payments/invoices/contracts/pricing.

payload.description: JSON body for create/update endpoints (non-money fields only).

path.description: Optional path-param dict for raw url mode.

method.description: HTTP method for raw url mode (default GET).

url.description: Relative URL for raw mode, e.g. '/api/agent/orders'.

tools.doc: dfd_bridge(action?, id?, orderId?, payload?, path?, method?, url?, timeout?) — Call the DFD Agency API bridge (NON-MONEY): leads, orders, milestones, notes, activities, client requests, projects, articles, whatsapp. Named actions (lead_list, order_get, milestone_create, note_create, activity_create, request_update, project_update, article_create, whatsapp_send) or raw method+url.

tools.name: create_client
tools.description: Create a client scaffold under D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects\<slug>\ (client.json + progress.md + mem/). REQUIRES explicit owner approval first (approved_by must be set). Never call without approval.

business_name.description: Client business name (slugified to folder name).

vertical.description: One of: fnb, salon, laundry, klinik, gym, bimbel, bengkel, beauty, travel, property, katering, photo.

approved_by.description: Who approved this scaffold (must be non-empty; the DFD agent sets it after owner approval).

order_id.description: DFD order id this client belongs to (optional).

tools.doc: create_client(business_name, vertical, features?, whatsapp?, domain?, approved_by?, order_id?) — Create client scaffold under D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects\<slug>\ (client.json + progress.md + mem/). REQUIRES explicit owner approval (approved_by).

tools.name: create_group
tools.description: Start a durable project that keeps working until it is done, across sessions and restarts, with its own folder, agents, tasks and board. Use when the goal is genuinely durable and multi-step. Do NOT use for a single self-contained request or for recurring work. Pass structured milestones and members — do not hand-write a manifest. Returns the project id and folder path; the effects are queued, so follow progress with group_board.

goal.description: The outcome wanted, one or two sentences.

milestones.description: Ordered phases. Each: {id, title, depends_on?, items:[{id, title, detail, acceptance:[...]}]}. Every item MUST have at least one acceptance criterion or it can never be completed.

members.description: Agents for this project. Each: {name, derived_from, model?, thinking?, tools?, skills?, mcp?}. Omit entirely for a single-agent project (the orchestrator does the work).

autonomy.description: Permission envelope, enforced. project_folder / external_read / external_write / destructive: autonomous | needs_approval | blocked. Work inside the project folder is always free; anything outside follows external_write, and needs_approval means the member parks and waits for the owner rather than failing — tell the owner that an outside action will need their approval. Also run_command: never | blocked | autonomous — never (the default) removes the shell from every member's toolset entirely, while blocked offers it and refuses dangerous commands at runtime. Set run_command to blocked or autonomous only for projects that genuinely need builds or tests; a member holding a shell can reach outside the project folder.

budget_usd.description: Hard spend ceiling. Enforced, not advisory.

deadline.description: ISO timestamp after which dispatch halts.

skills.description: Skill names to copy into the project.

mcp.description: MCP servers to attach (must already be installed on this machine).

project_id.description: Optional folder slug; otherwise derived from the goal.

tools.doc: create_group(goal, milestones, members?, autonomy?, completion?, budget_usd?, deadline?, skills?, mcp?, project_id?) — Start a durable project that runs until done, across restarts. Create only when the goal is genuinely durable; the orchestrator decides with high reasoning. Every item needs acceptance criteria. Queued; follow with group_board.

tools.name: group_board
tools.description: Snapshot only — not a polling tool. Group progress is event-driven; call once when the user asks for status, or before a final summary, then stop.
tools.doc: group_board(project_id) — one snapshot of milestones, items, statuses, spend, and approvals. Do not poll.

tools.name: group_item_detail
tools.description: Snapshot of one group item — not a polling tool. Call once when the user asks about it, then stop.
tools.doc: group_item_detail(project_id, item_id) — One item in full: attempts, latest result, and its acceptance criteria (why it passed or failed).

tools.name: group_events
tools.description: Snapshot of the project event log — not a polling tool. Call once when the user asks what happened, then stop.

since.description: Only events after this seq (for polling).

tools.doc: group_events(project_id, since?, limit?) — one snapshot of the event log. Do not poll.

tools.name: group_update
tools.description: Change a RUNNING project. One op per call, applied by the supervisor on its next tick (~15s), writing exactly one event. ops: add_item, add_milestone, invalidate_item, cancel_item, add_member, remove_member, attach_tool, attach_mcp, detach_mcp, attach_skill, detach_skill, pause, resume, close. 'invalidate_item' means the PLAN was wrong — not that the work failed; it does not count as a retry. Use it when a member reports an assumption turned out to be false. Read the result back with group_board.

params.description: Op arguments: e.g. {item_id, reason} for invalidate_item; {milestone_id, title, detail, acceptance} for add_item; {name, derived_from} for add_member; {server} for attach_mcp.

tools.doc: group_update(project_id, op, params?) — Change a RUNNING project: add_item, add_milestone, invalidate_item, cancel_item, add_member, remove_member, attach_tool, attach_mcp, detach_mcp, attach_skill, detach_skill, pause, resume, close. One op per call; queued until the next supervisor tick (~15s). invalidate_item = the PLAN was wrong, not that work failed.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description: Create a time-triggered wake for THIS orchestrator chat. When due, it appends a scheduled message and wakes the orchestrator even if the user has not spoken. Use for one-off alarms ('check the agents at 3pm') and recurring checks. This is the only way to create a schedule; there is no manual task UI.

at.description: ISO timestamp or HH:MM for the first run.

prompt.description: Instruction delivered to the orchestrator; defaults to name.

tools.doc: schedule(action?, name?, at?, prompt?, recurrence?, schedule_id?) — Create/list/cancel a time-triggered wake for this orchestrator chat. When due it appends a scheduled message and wakes the orchestrator. recurrence: none|daily|weekly|monthly|interval-<minutes>. No manual task UI.

tools.name: give_note
tools.description: Create or maintain a sticky note for a chat or group project. Notes are orchestrator-owned memory and UI checklists, not work items. Use todos for a checklist. Target is chat:<id> or group:<id>; omit it to use this chat.
tools.doc: give_note(action?, target?, title?, body?, todos?, note_id?) — Orchestrator-owned sticky note/checklist for chat:<id> or group:<id>. Actions create/update/remove/list. Notes are memory, not work items.

tools.name: canvas_mode
tools.description: Watch selected agent chats and wake the orchestrator when one finishes or fails. The orchestrator can choose one chat, several, or all agent chats. While active, a completion arrives as [CANVAS EVENT]; use canvas_mode read for the work snapshot and canvas_mode message to send a follow-up to a watched chat. Exit when done. This reads work state, never card coordinates.
tools.doc: canvas_mode(action?, mode?, targets?, wake_on?, max_actions?, until?, target?, message?) — Watch agent chats (single/multiple/all) and wake the orchestrator on completion/failure. available lists selectable chats/groups; read returns the work snapshot; message sends follow-up to a watched chat; exit stops watching.

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run a short JavaScript program that calls Stark tools directly. Use this for multi-step coding work: read or search several files, compute over the results, edit files, run commands, and return one compact result. Tool calls are synchronous: const text = tools.read_file({file_path: 'src/lib.rs'}); use JSON.parse(text) for structured output. Use search('query') to discover available tools. Programs have no filesystem, network, process, or import access except through tools. Not available in plan mode. Default limits: 30s, 50 tool calls, 32KB result.

code.description: JavaScript function body. Use return to send a JSON-serializable result.

tools.doc: run_code(code, timeout_ms?, max_tool_calls?) — Run a restricted JavaScript program that calls Stark tools. Use tools.<name>({...}) synchronously and return one compact value.

tools.name: agent
tools.description: Durable three-level agent control. spawn creates or reuses a workspace agent (or a subagent from a workspace agent) with a persisted mailbox task; list/status/send/report manage the tree. The server supervisor leases and runs agents, so work survives restarts and parent chats wake on results.

agent.description: Agent role, e.g. Developer, General, House, DFD, UI.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace id when the orchestrator spawns a workspace agent.

workspace_path.description: Target workspace path when the orchestrator spawns a workspace agent.

write_access.description: For subagent spawns: grant write access via an isolated worktree. Level-2 subagents are read-only by default.

isolate.description: Force git worktree isolation for this spawn.

tools.doc: agent(action, kind?, agent?, task?, title?, workspace_id?, workspace_path?, agent_id?, message?, quiet?, wait_seconds?) — Durable spawn/list/status/send/report for orchestrator → workspace → subagent.

tools.name: memory
tools.description: Read or update durable workspace memory. The compact MEMORY.md index is injected at run start; use this tool to read topic details, search entries, or explicitly remember/forget/pin a note.

topic.description: Topic name, e.g. decisions, facts, commands, pitfalls, preferences, tasks, notes.

scope.description: Memory tier: user (global across workspaces), project (current workspace, default), or session (this chat only).

tools.doc: memory(action?, topic?, query?, text?, kind?, entry_id?, pinned?) — Read/search durable workspace memory or add/forget/pin notes.

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description: Search MCP tools by keyword and enable them for the next request. Use this when a task needs a capability missing from the current tool list (for example GitHub, Supabase, browser automation, or deployment). Returns the matching tool schemas; call them by their full mcp__server__tool name afterwards.

query.description: Keywords describing the capability, e.g. "create github issue" or "query supabase table".

tools.doc: Search MCP tools by keyword and enable them for the next request. Use this when a task needs a capability missing from the current tool list (for example GitHub, Supabase, browser automation, or deployment). Returns the matching tool schemas; call them by their full mcp__server__tool name afterwards.
